contexts.text: How the serpent destroyed these lowest things with the antediluvians... will be told in what follows.
The antediluvian time is here treated of, and is understood by from afar, and by the days of antiquity.
This is the reason why the antediluvians were cast out of the garden of Eden, and vastated until they could acknowledge nothing that is true.
Under Most Ancient Church, see this reference.
The state of (the Postdiluvians) is altogether different from that of the antediluvians. Explained.
The state of these antediluvians is fully described in this verse...
The state of the antediluvians is treated of (in ).

As to what concerns the men of the antediluvian Church; in process of time they conceived direful persuasions, and immersed the goods and truths of faith in filthy cupidities, to such a degree that there were hardly any remains in them; and then they were as it were suffocated of their own accord. AC 563. AC 570. AC 579. AC 585. AC 594. AC 607:end. SE 3583.

That the antediluvians came at last to have almost no remains, was because they were of such a genius as to imbue direful and abominable persuasions about all things whatever that came up and fell into their thought, so that they would not by any means recede from them... supposing themselves to be as gods, and that whatever they thought was divine. Such a kind of persuasion never existed with any other nation either before or since, for it is deadly or suffocative; wherefore in the other life they can never be where other Spirits are. When they are present, they take away all faculty of thinking, by the influx of their most determined persuasions. AC 1034:end.
Violence is mentioned when violence is done to holy things by prophaning them, as these antediluvians did, who immersed the doctrinal things of faith in all kinds of cupidities.

That at the end of the days of the antediluvian Church all understanding of truth and will of good perished, is signified by these words... With the antediluvians who were imbued with direful persuasions and filthy cupidities they so perished that not a vestige of them appeared.
When the way for remains is closed up... the man is wholly possessed by evil Spirits... Hence was the death of the antediluvians, which is described by the flood.

By filthy cupidities and direful persuasions of falsity they blocked up the way of remains, so that they could not operate; such were the antediluvians who destroyed themselves, and who are understood by all flesh in which is the breath of lives, under the heavens.
To destroy every substance that I have made... = those who perished... Good and truth... were extinguished by tares with the antediluvians who perished.
From here to the end of this chapter the subject is concerning the antediluvians who perished.

The antediluvians... are here described as to persuasions; in the following verse as to cupidities; that is, as to the state of their intellectual things, and afterwards as to that of their voluntary things...
The persuasions of the antediluvians are here fully described; namely, that there were in them affections of falsity, cupidities, pleasures, corporeal and earthly.
The cupidities of the antediluvians were those of self-love...
With the antediluvians who perished not only was the Voluntary destroyed and made infernal, but the Intellectual also, so that they could not be regenerated...

At length in the last posterity of that Church, which was just before the Flood, hardly anything of inward breathing remained, and when it was at last annihilated in the breast, they were suffocated of their own accord.
There were with me some of the posterity that lived before the Flood, not of those who perished, but who were somewhat better than they. Described.
On the antediluvians who perished. General article. SE 3358. SE 3579.
(Antediluvian Spirits seen, who keep the thoughts bound; but not the Nephilim who perished.) SE 4183.

The antediluvians who perished are in a Hell under the heel of the left foot. They are covered over with a certain misty rock that breaks forth from their direful phantasies and persuasions; by which they are separated from the other Hells, and kept at a distance from the World of Spirits. They make a constant effort to rise up, but cannot advance beyond the endeavour. If they came into the World of Spirits, by their direful phantasies and the breathing and venom of their persuasions, they would take away the faculty of thinking from all the Spirits they met, except the good ones; and unless the Lord, by His coming in the flesh, had delivered the World of Spirits from that wicked crew, the human race would have perished; for there could not have been any Spirits with man. AC 1512. SE 4217.

Those of (the antediluvians) who persist in their attempts to emerge are cruelly treated by their companions, for they entertain deadly hatred against all, even against their companions; their highest delight consists in holding each other in subjection, and as it were in murdering each other. Those who persist the most strenuously in emerging are let down still deeper under that misty rock; for it is their insane ardour to destroy all that induces their efforts to emerge. (SE 4217.) They wrap all they meet in a piece of cloth, in order to take them captive; and cast them into a certain sea, as it appears to them, or otherwise entreat them savagely. SE 1270. SE 3365.

I was led, guarded, towards that misty rock... and conversed with them concerning their persuasions... They said they had persuaded themselves that there is no God, but that men are gods; thus that they were gods; and that they had confirmed themselves in this by their dreams. SE 3580, SE 3581, SE 3582. SE 4174.
(Some of the antediluvians permitted to ascend into the World of Spirits.) AC 1270. AC 1271. SE 3584.
Under Persuasion, see this reference, and at AC 1673.
(The dress of the antediluvian women. Their faces were small, but the men were shaggy and hairy. They prided themselves on the number of their children.) SE 3589.
(The nature of the antediluvians described.) Under Falsity, see this reference.
(On the modern antediluvians.) SE 3594. See also AC 1673:3.

Those who can profane good belong to the Celestial Church, for these can receive it even to perception. [This kind of profanation] was committed by the antediluvians, who are therefore kept secluded from all in a Hell that is separate from the Hells of others.
(The notion that the men of the Old Church will perish as the antediluvians did by the flood.)
(The antediluvians dwell beneath a great rock, deep below the buttocks, and treat the Lord most cruelly.) SE 3366.
(The antediluvians are not permitted to ascend, but the rock is sometimes attenuated, so that they can be heard...)
(The attempts of the antediluvians to emerge, and to be with others, so as to destroy them...) SE 3584.
(The antediluvians have not confirmed themselves against truths by reasonings, but it is their persuasion which acts, so that whatever they think is persuasive...) SE 3583.

Antediluvians who, on being vastated, can serve as subjects, retaining only so much life as there is in the bony parts of the human body. These were in the head; for those who are from the antediluvians are vastated, and become as skeletons, or as lifeless appendages, and life is afterwards breathed into them. Being scarcely aware of their own existence, or sensible, or conscious, they can thus serve for bones, into whom other Spirits can flow.
As the antediluvians lived in families they could dwell together with their married partners delightfully enough, yet (their marriages were merely a kind of adultery or lasciviousness). Explained.
(The antediluvians compared with the modern Nephilim or Sirens.) SE 4453. SE 4454. SE 4456.
(Situation of the Hells of the antediluvians; no one can be let into them; their efforts to murder each other.)

With those who descend into the Pit to the people of an age () = to those in Hell who were there from the Most Ancient Church immediately before the Flood. They are called the people of an age because they were of old time, and were in direful falsities above others.
